result.summary: Type E design artefact at src/design/iss0625-gh592-lua-12-15-16.md. Four irreversible decisions recorded: D-1 ExecutionContext gains *const ServiceCatalog + real HTTP path (simulation remains with defense-in-depth lookup); D-2 single response table per design §17.1 (breaking change, CHANGELOG note required); D-3 ScriptErrorPayload construction conditional on LUA-08 wiring in the same run (skip reason string otherwise); D-4 lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk requires new extern declarations in luajit_bindings.zig. Sequencing LUA-15 → LUA-12 → LUA-16 in three reviewable commits. Public interface covers ScriptResult.ErrorKind enum, ExecutionContext.service_catalog + instruction_limiter fields, host_context set/read/clearExplicitFailure helpers, events.buildScriptFailedPayload + buildScriptErrorPayload constructors. Data flow diagrams for each requirement. Error taxonomy lists all error sources and their ScriptResult mapping. Test plan per TC-LUA-12 (impl-01..10), TC-LUA-15 (impl-01..08), TC-LUA-16 (impl-01..08); HTTP client is a function-pointer stub in tests (T-1 compliance — no MSW/HTTP mocking). Per-test UUID fixture isolation mandatory. All decisions documented with rationale. Out-of-scope items explicit (engine-side worker, simulation interceptor internals, sibling batch 2 ExecutionContext fields). Implementation notes for BACKEND-DEV include the ScriptErrorPayload deinit-after-free pattern, EventRecord.deinit ownership, and the OQ-3 HTTP-client-resolution. No source code modified in this step.

issues.description: OQ-3: the production HTTP client (the function pointer that the real-call path invokes) is NOT introduced in this design. Tests use a Zig function pointer stub. In production the engine-side worker must inject the real HTTP client; if no such hook exists, this becomes a follow-up ISS. BACKEND-DEV should flag this during implementation if no hook is present in the engine.

D-3 means the test for the LUA-08 NOT-installed case asserts capabilities_at_failure equals the literal skip-reason string. Any future edit of that string is a test change. Consider extracting to a named constant in events.zig (e.g., SKIP_REASON_NO_INSTRUCTION_LIMITER) — left as a follow-up cleanup.

D-2 is a breaking change for any script written against the current (string, number) tuple return. CHANGELOG entry required (text drafted in §10.4). DOC-UPDATER (Step 6 of WF-03) must add the note alongside the requirement-status update.
